title: Dennis Allen, Press Taylor, Richard Hightower on Jeffery Simmons trade, preparing for Monday night vs. Seahawks | Press Conference
headline: Press Taylor says the Bears will replace Cole Kmet by committee and are leaning on Luther Burden III and Sam Roush, with Caleb Williams on an upswing, ahead of Monday night at Seattle.
summary: This was a joint session with Dennis Allen and Richard Hightower; Press Taylor's offensive answers start around 11:00. Taylor praised Caleb Williams's recent form, crediting his preparation and growth since last year, and said he has to back it up on Monday. He called Seattle's defense a challenge because of its versatility: it will play any look out of any personnel group, and its coverages disguise and rotate after the snap. He said the 300-plus-yard, 30-point passing game against New England left production on the field. Guys were getting open, but some throws were not made on time, and he singled out Luther Burden III's catch-and-run work. Taylor described Cole Kmet as a 'fixer' who did many jobs, and said replacing him means 'all hands on deck' rather than one next man up. Rookie tight end Sam Roush has progressed week to week, and Taylor hinted he could get more responsibility. On the backfield, he gave no specifics and described a committee and hot-hand approach that will be decided case by case. The question about Swift referred to missing a 'young guy' and the audio is garbled, so who is unavailable is unclear.

injuries.detail: Taylor talked about 'filling in for Cole' and replacing his many roles, which implies he is unavailable Monday. No injury details or timeline were given.
A reporter asked about not having 'a young guy' and managing D'Andre Swift's workload. The name was garbled and Taylor did not name anyone, so it is unclear who is out.

signals.claim: Williams is playing near his best since returning, but must repeat the preparation on Monday at Seattle.
signals.note: Taylor praised his accuracy and growth, which supports his fantasy outlook against a tough Seattle defense.
signals.quote: You've seen this growth in him from last year through the offseason

signals.claim: Kmet's many roles will be covered by multiple players rather than one replacement.
signals.note: The tight end workload will be spread out, which could raise Colston Loveland's and Sam Roush's usage but makes any single replacement hard to predict.
signals.quote: So it's all hands on deck to fill a role like that.

signals.claim: Roush may get more responsibility in the offense soon.
signals.note: With Kmet out, the rookie tight end could see a larger snap share, though Taylor was non-committal.
signals.quote: there's the opportunity maybe for some more on his plate

signals.claim: Burden will keep getting catch-and-run opportunities after his strong Thursday game.
signals.note: Taylor said his growth has been steady and praised his work on crossing routes, which points to continued target volume.
signals.quote: it's been a gradual growth with these guys

signals.claim: RB touches will be split by committee, with Swift's usage decided by game flow and need in pass protection.
signals.note: Taylor gave no clear workload commitment for Swift, so backfield volume is uncertain.

topics.detail: Taylor said Seattle's versatility is the biggest challenge. They play any coverage from any personnel group, start in a shell, and rotate coverage based on what the offense does, so Chicago needs a standard response to every look.

The offense passed for 300-plus yards and scored 30 points, but Taylor said there was 'meat on the bone'. Some open throws were not delivered on time, including a first-down misfire where the timing and footwork were off.
The acquisition of Jeffery Simmons gave the building a lift. Taylor said he was glad not to face him anymore and joked about finding him a goal-line pass.

title: Brian Fleury On The Addition Of Quenton Nelson, Preparing For Week 8
headline: Quenton Nelson joins at guard and Grey Zabel moves to right guard with Charles Cross out. Fleury says the offense will keep spreading the ball to tight ends like AJ Barner because defenses are focusing on Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
summary: Fleury said the mini-bye let the offense narrow its plan to what it already did well. That produced strong third-down numbers and better protection for Sam Darnold. He credited Jake Peetz, Leslie Frazier and John Benton for a quick-passing third-down plan built to beat that specific defense. Quick throws will stay a big part of the offense, but each week's plan will vary. The line is in flux: Quenton Nelson arrives, Grey Zabel flips to right guard next to Abraham Lucas, and Charles Cross is out. Fleury's main concerns are communication and terminology, so Nelson's early workload will be kept light. He called Jaxon Smith-Njigba an incredible teammate who is happy to share the ball, and said the team is deliberately getting others involved, including AJ Barner, because opponents are trying to take Smith-Njigba away. Anthony Bradford loses his starting spot but will stay in the game plans, including the extra-lineman 'barnyard' short-yardage package, which was used three times on fourth-and-short. Fleury also said the offense carries contingency plans, and he had to shuffle personnel when Rashid Shaheed and another speed player left the game.

injuries.detail: Fleury referred to Cross being out, forcing Grey Zabel to move to right guard. The injury report lists Cross as DNP with an ankle injury.
Fleury said Shaheed left the last game and the staff had to shuffle people to keep his plays available. The injury report lists him as a full practice participant with a knee issue.

signals.claim: Nelson will step into the starting guard spot, with a limited playbook early on.
signals.note: His arrival reshapes the line and should help pass protection over time, but a short-term communication learning curve is expected.

signals.claim: Zabel will play right guard next to Abraham Lucas instead of beside Charles Cross.
signals.note: A side change brings some early communication risk for the line, though Fleury expects it to smooth out quickly.
signals.quote: I'm sure the learning curve will evaporate pretty quickly.

signals.claim: Bradford will no longer start but will stay involved in game plans, including packages with extra offensive linemen.
signals.note: His role shrinks to situational snaps, so he has little fantasy relevance beyond short-yardage packages.
signals.quote: There's going to be ways to keep Anthony involved.

signals.claim: Tight ends, Barner in particular, will be a bigger emphasis in the passing game going forward.
signals.note: The coaching staff is deliberately feeding Barner as defenses take away Smith-Njigba, which supports his target outlook.
signals.quote: there's been a deliberate approach to try and get everybody a little bit more involved.

signals.claim: Opponents will keep trying to take Smith-Njigba away, and the offense will deliberately spread targets to others.
signals.note: He is still the focal point, but his target share could be capped if the team distributes the ball more.
signals.quote: he also understands the value in distributing it to his teammates

signals.claim: The offense will keep using a quick-passing game and protection plans to get Darnold the ball out fast.
signals.note: Quick throws and better protection support his efficiency, though the exact approach will vary each week.
signals.quote: the third down plan that would allow us to get the ball out quickly

signals.claim: Shaheed left the previous game, and the offense had to rearrange personnel to keep his plays available.
signals.note: He is a speed player the offense plans around, so his health matters for deep-ball and gadget usage.
signals.quote: with Sheed and Bayless going out, those were two of our kind of speed players

topics.detail: The staff leaned on things the offense already executed well after reviewing the first six games. The quick-game approach was tailored to that defense.
The extra-lineman package was used three times in fourth-and-short situations. It requires precise alignment and set-up, and it was already in the plan before this game.
Fleury is trimming volume week to week because the group is new to the system. Contingency plans remain for injuries.

title: Brian Daboll Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Daboll praised Cam Ward's work ethic and credited a well-blocked run game for Tony Pollard's big game, but gave no injury or role news ahead of the Bengals.
summary: Daboll was asked about Cam Ward's slow starts and better fourth quarters. He gave no specific reason, saying only that Ward is his own biggest critic and is working on communication, protections, mechanics and footwork. He stressed that improvement has to come from all 11 players, not just the quarterback. He said the offensive line is getting better, pointing to a lower sack total than last year, and credited Ward for identifying protections and getting the ball out quickly. He wouldn't commit to a run-heavy identity. He wants the offense to be 'more productive,' and said last week's run-first approach was specific to that game plan. He explained Tony Pollard's strong run game by saying the line and receivers blocked well and the gap/trap concepts worked. Tight ends have been used a lot in protection and as jammers, and he will keep doing that if needed. The screen game has been held back by defensive fronts that didn't play as expected. Daboll singled out Bengals DT Dexter Lawrence as the biggest challenge, said he hasn't thought about bye-week self-scouting yet, and gave no injury updates.

signals.claim: Ward will keep improving his protections, mechanics and footwork, but Daboll offered no explanation for the fourth-quarter splits.
signals.note: Daboll sidestepped the slow-start question, so expect continued inconsistency early in games, with quick-game and protection work supporting him.
signals.quote: he's working his tail off to try to get better each and every day

signals.claim: Daboll would like to repeat the successful run game, but the last game's run-heavy plan was game-plan specific.
signals.note: Pollard's big game was tied to blocking and a specific game plan, so a repeat depends on matchup and scheme and is not guaranteed.
signals.quote: was blocked well and he ran well

topics.detail: Daboll says the line has improved as the year has gone on, with fewer sacks than last year. He credits Ward's pre-snap identification and quick release for part of that.
Tight ends have stayed in to block and jam quite a bit, helping on edges on longer-developing and run-action plays. Daboll says that will continue if needed, which limits their receiving upside.
A recent screen opportunity failed because the defensive front played differently than expected. Daboll says screens remain part of the offense, but read-and-react linemen make them harder to run.
Daboll declined to commit to a run-heavy identity and said he wants the offense to be more productive however it gets there. He described last week's approach as game-plan specific.
Daboll hasn't thought much about the bye week yet. He says the team normally reviews its tendencies over several games, and that will happen then.
